sourceArticle.title: My Obsidian notes are now a live website — one free plugin set it up in under an hour
sourceArticle.author: Tashreef Shareef

athenaOutput.directive: Establish the Obsidian vault as the sovereign, immutable source of truth for the Creative Liberation Engine's knowledge base, utilizing an automated, zero-friction pipeline to publish a self-hosted digital garden.
athenaOutput.rationale: The discovery of a single-plugin publishing workflow for Obsidian perfectly aligns with our core tenets. It bridges local, sovereign thought-capture (Obsidian) with public or team-wide distribution without relying on proprietary SaaS platforms. By routing this capability through our NAS (Forgejo/CI) rather than third-party clouds, we achieve Article I (Sovereignty) and Article XX (Zero human wait time), ensuring the artist's knowledge graph is instantly live, fully owned, and architecturally sound.

options.title: The Sovereign Digital Garden (NAS-Hosted Static Site)
options.description: Utilize a free open-source static site generator plugin (e.g., Quartz, MkDocs, or Obsidian Digital Garden) configured to push directly to the local Forgejo instance on the NAS. A Forgejo Action automatically builds and deploys the site to a self-hosted Nginx container.
options.tradeoffs: Requires initial CI/CD pipeline setup on the NAS and proper Nginx routing. However, it guarantees 100% data ownership, zero recurring costs, and infinite customizability without vendor lock-in.

options.title: The Agentic Knowledge Base (RAG-Enabled)
options.description: The published website isn't just static markdown; it integrates locally-hosted LLMs (via the Creative Liberation Engine's model ops) to allow visitors or team members to 'chat' with the Obsidian vault using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation).
options.tradeoffs: High computational overhead for the NAS to run embedding models and LLMs for web visitors. Massive increase in utility and interactivity, transforming passive reading into active inquiry.

options.title: Obsidian as a Headless CMS
options.description: Bypass standard static site generators. Use a plugin to export the vault as structured JSON/Markdown via an API or Git sync, which is then consumed by a bespoke React 19 / Next.js frontend built by BOLT and AURORA.
options.tradeoffs: Heavier development lift to build the frontend from scratch (violates 'under an hour' constraint initially). Provides absolute control over UI/UX and allows complex interactive components (e.g., 3D data visualizations of the knowledge graph).

options.title: The Real-Time Broadcast Wiki
options.description: Integrate the Obsidian publishing pipeline directly into the BROADCAST hive. When a note is updated, WebSockets push the changes live to streaming overlays, dashboards, or connected client screens instantly.
options.tradeoffs: Niche application primarily useful for live events, streams, or command centers. May overcomplicate standard documentation reading experiences.

options.title: Third-Party Cloud Deployment (Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare)
options.description: Use the plugin's default configuration to push the Obsidian vault to a commercial edge network or proprietary hosting provider for instant global CDN distribution.
options.tradeoffs: Extremely fast setup, but fundamentally violates Article I (Sovereignty) and Article XXIII (Biometric/Data Sovereignty) by placing the core knowledge graph on rented infrastructure subject to external terms of service.

options.title: The Collaborative Hive Mind (Git-Backed Community PRs)
options.description: Publish the site with an integrated annotation and 'Edit on Forgejo' layer. The site serves as a read-only view, but authenticated users can propose pull requests directly to the markdown source, turning personal notes into a community-driven engine.
options.tradeoffs: Introduces moderation overhead and complex Git conflict resolution for non-technical users. Excellent for open-source projects or collaborative world-building.
